title: Dispatch OGF 4: Surveyors Find Glass Threads in Reservoir Wall
summary: The orchard’s roots lead toward masonry that protects the northern quarter.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: City surveyors yesterday found translucent threads running through a drainage channel beneath the Northmere Reservoir. The threads continue in the direction of Rill Orchard. A sample cut from the channel has the brittle surface of glass and the branching structure of a root.

The reservoir wall is sound by ordinary inspection. Inspector Daniel Voss, who supervised the survey, warns that the threads may open the mortar if they continue to widen. He has ordered daily measurements. The first comparison shows movement too small to judge after one day.

On Mrs. Rill’s land, Dr. Saye traced the threads to the oldest mirrorwood graft. Peter’s notebook describes the cutting as “able to hold an impression after the witness departs.” He had hoped to preserve the orchard as it looked while his father was alive. The notebook says nothing about taking images from other people or growing roots into stone.

Dr. Saye proposes that the graft draws scenes from nearby lives and possible events through the Eidetic Stratum. She has not established that the fruit causes the future it displays. The damaged channel, however, gives the city an immediate danger it can measure without trusting the images.

Alderman Dorne has ordered the northern reservoir lowered by one third and preparations made to move residents below it if the wall changes. Mrs. Rill has offered to let the city remove the graft. Dr. Saye asks for two days to learn whether cutting it would leave the threads intact inside the masonry.
